## [I rebuilt my game studio website with Claude Code and I think web dev is cooked](https://reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1tf0iqm/i_rebuilt_my_game_studio_website_with_claude_code/)
*Reddit r/ClaudeAI* | 16/05/2026 | Score: 0.62
Tags: gaming_platform

> I'm an indie game developer, not a web developer. I needed to update the website for my studio and I wanted something that actually felt like a *game studio* — so I designed the layout inspired by game UI menus. Clean sections, navigation that feels intentional, that kind of thing. A few iterations in Claude and I had it all working locally. Then I did something I've never done before: I just handed Claude Code my SSH credentials and let it deploy. It connected to my server, pushed everything, and the site was live. I didn't touch a single terminal command. But the part that genuinely surprised me: it also built a data layer that pulls live info from the Steam API — game details, screenshots, Workshop content — and structures it so it works across all our titles automatically. It's responsive on mobile too. The result: [**speedrivals.es**](http://speedrivals.es) I've shipped games. I know what it feels like when something clicks. This clicked. I don't say this lightly: I think the profession of "web developer" as most studios hire it is effectively over. At least for projects at this scale.
